scoring_justification: The headline quantities (adsorption energies, barriers, charges, ICOHP) are DFT-computed and cannot be recomputed from lightweight artifacts; the verifier compares the agent's reported values to the paper's hidden gold with tolerances and trend ordering. The pCOHP curve is audited structurally and its peak positions are compared to hidden gold.

hidden_assets.purpose: Gold reference values for adsorption, activation, charges, ICOHP, and pCOHP peak energies
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper Tables 2, 3, 4, and Figure 6; cross-checked with reference solution solve.sh.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Numerical values extracted from the paper and encoded as hardcoded inline gold; solve.sh produces exactly these numbers.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: Values are directly from the paper's reported data tables and figures for these three surfaces.

schema.notes: One row per surface. Values compared to hidden reference values with tolerances.

outputs.description: Machine-readable table of computed adsorption energies, Bader charges, activation barriers, and metal–CH3 ICOHP for the three surfaces.

schema.notes: Data must cover at least -15 to +5 eV. Checker audits structural features (presence of bonding peak below E_F and unoccupied peak in 1-2 eV).

outputs.description: The -pCOHP spectrum for the activated C-H bond on IrO₂(110).

schema.pattern: Occupied bonding peak at {value} eV; Unoccupied bonding peak at {value} eV.
schema.notes: Peak energies compared to hidden reference within ±0.25 eV tolerance.

outputs.description: Plain-text statement of the key pCOHP peak energies.

output_contract.notes: The adsorption_results.csv values are compared to the paper-reported figures with appropriate tolerances; relative trends are also enforced. The pCOHP curve is structurally audited, and peak positions are verified via the second file.
